correctness.rationale: For a finite projection P the two squared leakage norms sum to the squared unnormalized Hilbert–Schmidt commutator norm, and their signed difference is the compressed trace of T*T−TT*. For the shift model this compressed trace tends to p−q for every strong exhaustion, giving the required lower bound without assuming nestedness. Pairing a forward and backward copy gives the bilateral shift after adding one matrix unit. Dyadic arc-constant projections increase strongly to the identity; on each arc the compressed multiplier has modulus sinc(π/N), so both leakages have total squared norm 2N(1−sinc²(π/N))→0. Each unpaired copy contributes a single boundary matrix unit to the direct-sum nested sequence, attaining |p−q| in squared norm. For any strong exhaustion by self-adjoint contractions, multiplication of I−R_n against a Hilbert–Schmidt K tends to zero in Hilbert–Schmidt norm on both sides by finite-rank approximation; this proves invariance sequence by sequence. The diagonal ramp with N jumps of size 1/N has squared cost (p+q)/N, hence the ordinary positive-contraction modulus vanishes. The index q−p follows from kernel and cokernel dimensions and compact-perturbation invariance. This covers also the balanced and pure one-sign cases. The frozen diagnostic is supplementary; the review used the analytic identities, not a run of that script.

value.rationale: Forward/backward shifts are canonical index models, and the least commutator leakage for projection cutoffs is a natural approximation invariant. The law quantifies exactly how the two signs cancel and separates this projection cost from a zero cost under positive contractions. An exact dimension-free floor, not just existence or nonexistence of approximate commutation, is useful in testing what information projection approximations can retain.
